Create a roughViz widget

Source: R/roughViz.R
roughViz.Rd

Low level constructor that powers all exported chart helpers in **roughVizR**. Most users will call a convenience wrapper such as [roughBar()] or [roughScatter()], but this function can be handy when you already have a fully formed configuration list.

Usage

roughViz(chartType, config, width = NULL, height = NULL, elementId = NULL)

Arguments

chartType

Character string naming the roughViz.js chart to render (e.g. `"Bar"`, `"Pie"`, `"Scatter"`). See <https://github.com/jwilber/roughViz> for the complete catalogue.

config

Named list describing the chart configuration. The list should normally include a `data` entry (either a `data.frame` or a nested list matching the roughViz.js API) along with any visual options accepted by the corresponding JavaScript chart.

width

Optional width passed to [htmlwidgets::createWidget()]. Supply a numeric value (pixels) or valid CSS units (character strings). When omitted the widget scales responsively.

height

Optional height passed to [htmlwidgets::createWidget()]. Supply a numeric value (pixels) or valid CSS units (character strings). When omitted the widget scales responsively.

elementId

Optional DOM id to target when embedding the widget in a larger document.

Value

An [`htmlwidgets::htmlwidget`] ready for printing or embedding.

Details

The helper functions exported by the package build up the `config` list for you, validating column names and coercing values where appropriate. When calling `roughViz()` directly it is your responsibility to follow the roughViz.js schema. Any additional arguments are ignored; use the `config` list to supply custom settings.

Passing additional options

Every chart accepts a `...` argument in its helper that is appended to the configuration list after validation. This makes it possible to reach new options introduced by roughViz.js without waiting for a package update.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  roughViz(
    chartType = "Bar",
    config = list(
      data = list(
        labels = c("A", "B", "C"),
        values = c(3, 5, 2)
      ),
      title = "Quick sketch"
    )
  )
}
